paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God is King of all the earth, and that is why this psalm cannot stay quiet. It says, "God is King of all the earth; sing to Him a psalm of praise." (Psalm 47:7) Not some of the earth. ALL of it, and that means every people on it gets invited to clap.

Now look at what this King does for His people. The psalm says, "He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves." (Psalm 47:4) Your future isn't something you have to scramble and grab for like the last cookie on the cooling rack. The King who reigns over everything is the One who chooses it, and He chooses it with love.

And the psalm doesn't end with one nation. It ends with "The nobles of the nations have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham," (Psalm 47:9) so the invitation reaches way past one nation. So when life gets loud and everything feels up for grabs, remember who is seated on the throne. Then do what the psalm says: sing praises, friend. I'll be right here with my mustache clapping.
